title: Invariant affine neighbourhoods of codimension-one finite groupoid orbits
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in $K$-schemes [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Assume $s,t:R\to U$ are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $U$ is separated over $K$ and locally Noetherian [def-weil-proper-morphism, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $u\in U$, and let $O(u)$ be its orbit, the set of points $t(r)$ for points $r\in R$ with $s(r)=u$; field-valued points may be compared after a common field extension. Assume $\dim\mathcal O_{U,v}\leq1$ for every $v\in O(u)$, where $\mathcal O_{U,v}$ is the structure-sheaf stalk and ring dimension is [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then there is an affine open subscheme $W\subseteq U$ [def-pc-scheme] with $O(u)\subseteq W$ and $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$ as open subschemes of $R$.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1); the field-relative separatedness implies absolute separatedness because Spec K is separated.

proof.text: The identity, inverse and composition laws make $O=t(s^{-1}(\{u\}))$ an equivalence class of points: for composition choose a common extension of the two residue fields over the common intermediate point. The finite fibre of $s$ shows that $O$ is finite. Every affine open of $U$ has Noetherian coordinate ring, and each stalk is a localization of such a ring, hence Noetherian. Locally finite irreducible components imply that a quasi-compact open meets only finitely many components (take a finite subcover of the witnessing neighbourhoods). The diagonal of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ over $\mathbf Z$ is closed: its affine ring map $K\otimes_{\mathbf Z}K\to K$ is surjective, since $a$ is the image of $a\otimes1$. The map $U\times_KU\to U\times_{\mathbf Z}U$ is its base change. Composing this closed immersion with the given relative diagonal proves absolute separatedness of $U$. Apply the common-affine-neighbourhood lemma to the finite set $O$, using its assumed local dimension bound, to obtain an affine open $A_0\subseteq U$ containing $O$.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), first paragraph, finite orbit and common affine neighbourhood (Tag 09NN)

proof.text: Set $C=t(s^{-1}(U\setminus A_0))$. It is closed because $s$ is continuous and $t$ is closed. It is a union of orbits by inverse and composition. An orbit meeting $U\setminus A_0$ cannot be $O$, so $O\cap C=\varnothing$. The identity arrow gives $U\setminus A_0\subseteq C$. Thus $U_0=U\setminus C$ is an invariant open containing $O$ and contained in $A_0$. The Noetherian scheme $A_0$ has Noetherian open subscheme $U_0$. Restriction to this invariant open is harmless: any invariant open of $U_0$ is open and invariant in $U$. Henceforth replace $U$ by $U_0$; it has an immersion into an affine scheme and is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), first paragraph, closed saturation and quasi-affine reduction

proof.text: Apply integral orbit-cover descent to the reduction $U_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow U$: it is a closed immersion and hence integral, its underlying map is the identity, and it meets every orbit. The restricted groupoid still has finite source and target. In general for a closed immersion $T\hookrightarrow U$, its restricted arrow scheme is $T\times_U R\times_U T$; its source is the composite of a closed immersion into $R\times_{s,U}T$ with the finite base change of $s$, and similarly for the target. This composite is finite: on affine charts a quotient of a finite module is finite. Reduction preserves the prime chains and the local dimension bounds. It therefore suffices to work with reduced $U$, remembering to descend the final invariant affine back to the original $U$.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), second paragraph, reduction via Tag 0ABE

proof.text: Choose the invariant open $W$ and closed thickening $W\prime\subseteq W$ of the almost-dense-flat-locus lemma. Since $W$ is reduced, the ideal of a closed subscheme with the same underlying space is zero: on each reduced affine chart its elements lie in every prime and hence in the zero nilradical. Thus $W\prime=W$, so the restricted maps on $W$ are finite locally free. Put $T=\overline{|W|}_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its inclusion is integral, and $U=t(s^{-1}(|T|))$ says precisely that it meets every orbit. Choose $u\prime\in O(u)\cap T$ and apply integral orbit-cover descent once more. Proving the result on $T$ suffices, since the descended invariant open contains $u\prime$, hence all of $O(u)$. Closed-subscheme local rings are quotients, so their prime chains are a subset of the original chains and the dimension bounds persist. Replace $U$ by $T$, $u$ by $u\prime$, and restrict the groupoid; now $W$ is dense as well as open, invariant, and finite locally free for the restricted groupoid.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), second paragraph, almost dense locus (0ABA) and closed reduction (0ABE)

proof.text: All replacements are closed subschemes of the preceding Noetherian scheme and retain an immersion into an affine scheme; finite type quotient charts are Noetherian, and closed subsets of quasi-compact spaces are quasi-compact. Their source and target maps remain finite by the restricted-arrow calculation above. If $u\in W$, its entire orbit lies in $W$. The common-affine-neighbourhood lemma applies inside the separated locally Noetherian open $W$, with the same local rings at orbit points and finitely many irreducible components on quasi-compact opens. Then finite-locally-free invariant-affine shrinking gives the required invariant affine in $W$ and hence in $U$. The remembered integral descents finish this case. Otherwise $O(u)\cap W=\varnothing$; assume this case for the remaining steps.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), third paragraph, the case u in W (03JE)

proof.text: Consider every strict generalization $\xi$ of any $v\in O(u)$. The local dimension bound implies that $\xi$ has no strict generalization: a chain $\eta\leadsto\xi\leadsto v$ would give a length-two prime chain in $\mathcal O_{U,v}$. Thus $\xi$ is a component generic point: a component through $\xi$ exists by the component-cover lemma, and its unique generic point (scheme sobriety) generalizes $\xi$, hence equals $\xi$. It lies in the dense open $W$; it is outside $O(u)$ by orbit incomparability. There are finitely many such points $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_m$, because the Noetherian scheme $U$ has finitely many irreducible components. The list may be empty.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), third paragraph, strict generalizations of the distinguished orbit

proof.text: The $R_W$-orbit of each $\xi_j$ consists of component generic points. As in step 6, a point of a scheme is a component generic point exactly when it has no proper generalization (component-cover lemma and sobriety; conversely, the closure of a generalization of a component generic point contains that component, so maximality and uniqueness of generic points force equality). Choose an arrow $r$ with $s_W(r)=\xi_j$. Any generalization $r\prime$ of $r$ has $s_W(r\prime)$ a generalization of $\xi_j$, hence $s_W(r\prime)=\xi_j$; on affine charts of the finite, hence integral, map $s_W$, integral incomparability forces $r\prime=r$. Thus $r$ has no proper generalization. Let $v$ be a generalization of $t_W(r)$. Since $t_W$ is finite locally free, hence flat by definition, flat generalization lifting gives $r\prime$ generalizing $r$ with $t_W(r\prime)=v$; then $r\prime=r$ and $v=t_W(r)$. So $t_W(r)$ has no proper generalization in $W$, nor in $U$, because a generalization in $U$ of a point of the open $W$ lies in $W$. Hence $t_W(r)$ is a generic point of an irreducible component of $W$ and of $U$.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), third paragraph, generic orbits under finite locally free maps

proof.text: Fix an immersion $j:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ inherited from the preceding replacements. Let $H=\overline{j(U)}$. The image $j(U)$ is open in $H$, and $j(W)$ is open in $j(U)$, hence open in $H$. Choose ideals $I,J\subseteq A$ with $V(I)=H\setminus j(U)$ and $V(J)=H\setminus j(W)$; these are closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Thus $V(I)\cup j(U)=H$, $V(J)\cup j(W)=H$, and both required disjointness conditions hold. The finite maps on the locally Noetherian schemes $U$ and $W$ are of finite presentation. Apply the almost-invariant-function lemma to $W$, $j|_W$, $J$, and the list $\xi_j$. It gives $f\in J$ with $F=j^{-1}D(f)\subseteq W$ affine and invariant, containing all $\xi_j$. The inclusion follows because $j(U\setminus W)\subseteq V(J)$; invariance in $W$ and invariance of $W$ imply invariance in $U$.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), fourth paragraph, boundary ideal and almost invariant f (0ABF)

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $U\setminus F=j^{-1}V(f)$. Its underlying set is a union of orbits, although $Z$ need not be scheme-theoretically invariant. Restrict the groupoid using $R_Z=Z\times_U R\times_U Z$. Its maps are finite by the closed-immersion/finite-base-change calculation in step 3. Over common field extensions this restriction retains exactly the arrows whose endpoints lie in $Z$, so the $R_Z$-orbit of $u$ is precisely $O(u)$. Every strict generalization of a point of $O(u)$ was among the $\xi_j$ and belongs to $F$. There are therefore no strict generalizations inside $Z$ at any orbit point: all points of $O(u)$ are generic points of components of $Z$. This proves the local dimension-zero assertion directly from the prime chains.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), fifth paragraph, reduced closed complement and dimension drop

proof.text: The finite groupoid on $Z$ is of finite presentation, since $Z$ is locally Noetherian. Restrict $j$ to $Z$. The ideal $I$ from step 8 is disjoint from $j(Z)$ and $V(I)\cup j(Z)$ is closed: it is the complement of the open $j(F)$ in $H$. Apply the almost-invariant-function lemma to this immersion, $I$, and the point $u$, whose whole orbit is now generic in $Z$. Obtain $h\in I$ such that $Z_h=Z\cap j^{-1}D(h)$ is affine, invariant for the restricted groupoid, and contains $O(u)$. No scheme-theoretic invariance of $Z$ in $U$ was assumed or used.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), sixth paragraph, almost invariant h on the closed complement (0ABF)

proof.text: Work only on the invariant affine $F\subseteq W$. Its arrow scheme $R_F$ is affine since its source $s_F$ is finite and $F$ is affine. Form the determinant norm $g=\operatorname{Norm}_{s_F}(t_F^*(j^*h|_F))\in\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_F)$. The norm-chart theorem constructs it even with varying local rank. The affine groupoid norm lemma makes $g$ invariant. The prime norm criterion, applied on the finite free charts, says that $g(x)\ne0$ exactly when $h(t(r))\ne0$ for every arrow $r$ with $s(r)=x$. The identity arrow then gives $F_g\subseteq j^{-1}D(h)$. Invariance of $g$ gives invariance of $F_g$ in $F$ and thus in $U$. Moreover $F_g$ is affine, being the principal open of the affine scheme $F$.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), seventh paragraph, determinant norm (03BH), restricted to the affine F

proof.text: Set $V=F_g\cup Z_h$ as a subset of $U$. It contains $O(u)$ and is a union of orbits, since $F$ and its complement $|Z|$ are invariant and each of the two pieces is invariant for the corresponding restriction. It is constructible: $F_g$ is open and $Z_h$ is locally closed in the Noetherian space $U$. To show $V$ open we check stability under generalization; $F_g$ already is open, so only a specialization $x\leadsto z$ with $z\in Z_h$ needs consideration. If $x\in Z$, nonvanishing of $h$ at $z$ implies its nonvanishing at $x$, so $x\in Z_h$.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), seventh paragraph, definition of V and first generalization case

proof.text: If instead $x\notin Z$, then $x\in F$. Suppose $x\notin F_g$. The norm criterion supplies $r_1\in R_F$ with $s(r_1)=x$ and $h(t(r_1))=0$. Since $s:R\to U$ is closed, the closed-map specialization lemma lifts $x\leadsto z$ to $r_1\leadsto r_2$ with $s(r_2)=z$. The zero locus of the global section $j^*h$ is closed, so $h(t(r_2))=0$. But $t(r_2)$ is in the orbit of $z$, hence in $Z_h$ by invariance there; this contradicts its zero value of $h$. Therefore every such $x$ lies in $F_g$, establishing stability under generalization. On each affine chart of $U$ the constructible subset $V$ is now generalization stable, so the spectrum constructibility lemma makes it open. These local opens show that $V$ is open in $U$.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), seventh paragraph, specialization lifting proves openness of V

proof.text: We have $V\subseteq j^{-1}D(h)$, hence an immersion $j\prime:V\to\operatorname{Spec}A_h$. It is quasi-compact, since $V$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian $U$. For the image $f\prime\in A_h$ of $f$, its inverse-image principal open is $F_g$, which is affine. Also $j\prime(V)\cap V(f\prime)=j(Z_h)$ is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A_h$: the equality $V(I)\cup j(U)=H$ and $h\in I$ imply $j(U)\cap D(h)=H\cap D(h)$, closed in $D(h)$, and intersecting with $V(f)$ gives exactly $j(Z_h)$. Apply the immersion-principal-affineness criterion to $(j\prime,f\prime)$ to obtain that $V$ is affine. It is invariant and contains $O(u)$. Finally apply the two integral orbit-cover descents remembered in steps 3 and 4, and include the resulting open into the original invariant open from step 2. This gives the asserted affine $W$ in the original $U$ with equality of source and target inverse-image opens.

source.place: Tag 0ABI (lemma-find-affine-codimension-1), last paragraph, affineness by 0ABH and descent back to the original scheme
